The relative speed between the ejecta and the Galactic center is \(v = 60\,000\ \text{km/s} = 0.2c\) (with \(c = 300\,000\ \text{km/s}\)). In the ejecta's rest frame, a proper time interval of \(\Delta \tau = 50\ \text{s}\) passes. The corresponding time interval in the Galaxy frame is dilated: \(\Delta t = \gamma \Delta \tau\), where \(\gamma = 1/\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2} = 1/\sqrt{1 - 0.04} = 1/\sqrt{0.96} \approx 1.02\). Thus \(\Delta t \approx 51\ \text{s}\). The distance traveled by the ejecta in the Galaxy frame is \(d = v \Delta t \approx 60\,000 \times 51 = 3\,060\,000\ \text{km}\).

Answer: D
